Judgment

The petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to the 2nd respondent to consider
Ext.P7 request made by him within a time limit to be fixed by this Court and also for a direction to
the
3rd respondent to conduct an auction sale of the property which was acquired from the petitioner in Survey No.12/34 of Elampalloor Village.
2. The petitioner is absolute owner and in possession of a total extent of 30 cents of property in Survey No.12/34 of Elampalloor Village, Kollam Taluk, Kollam District.

In the year 1992, for the purpose of construction of a distributary canal called Mulavana Distributary as part of Kallada Irrigation Project, Section 4(1) notification under Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued by the Acquiring Authority for acquiring a total extent of 0.52.83 Hectares of land in Elampalloor Village.
5.80 Ares of land owned by the petitioner out of the total extent of 30 cents in Sy.No.12/34 was also included in the said notification.

Petitioner further submits that after acquisition of land, Irrigation Department abandoned the project and petitioner along with others submitted application for reconveyance of the property to the 1st respondent and thereafter approached this Court filing WP(C) No.22914/2015, which was disposed of as per Ext.P3 judgment directing the Government to examine whether the land could be returned to the petitioner on refunding the entire compensation received along with interest.

Pursuant to the direction issued by this Court, the 1st respondent heard the aggrieved persons and passed Ext.P4 order wherein a decision was taken to dispose of the property by conducting public auction of the property acquired from the petitioner and other land owners.
Ext.P4 order was challenged before this Court in WP(C) No.13028/2020.

In the meanwhile,
notice for public auction was issued by the 3rd respondent in respect of the property covered by Ext.P4 order.

In the auction the properties in Survey Nos.12/33 and 12/39 owned by the petitioner in WP(C) No.22793/2015 which was disposed of along with Ext.P3 judgment owned by Geevarghese Yohannan was bidded in auction for an amount of Rs.59,55,000/-.

Though the petitioner sought for interim relief staying all further proceedings pursuant to the public auction, this Court as per interim order dated 27.10.2021 permitted the respondents to proceed with the auction and directed the 1 st petitioner in WP(C) No.13028/2020 to inform this Court whether he is willing to match the highest bid obtained through the said process with a minor escalation.

Thereupon, the 1st petitioner in Ext.P5 interim order submitted his willingness to remit the highest bid amount for the property in Sy.Nos.12/33 and 12/39 of Elampalloor Village, which was acquired from him.

But as regard the property of the petitioner is concerned, despite conduct of three public auctions dated 11.3.2022,
18.4.2022 and 7.5.2022
, no one bid the property and the respondents are not taking any further steps in this regard.
Petitioner contend that due to the acquisition, the property is divided into two parts like triangles since the land taken is along the diagonal of a square shaped land which can be seen from Ext.P2.
It is the said circumstance the petitioner has approached this Court seeking the reliefs.

In Ext.P7 the request made by the petitioner, is to earmark 3 metres width land on the northern part of acquired land for access to the property of the petitioner and to fix the value of that Alex Thomas P.G.T., Represented By ... vs State Of Kerala on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17222483/
2 extent of land enabling the petitioner to get ingress and egress to the rear part of the land after acquisition.
Petitioner would submit that this request as per Ext.P7 has been turned down by the respondents.

Petitioner now submits that he is only pressing for relief No.ii wherein a direction was sought to the 3rd respondent to conduct auction sale of property which was acquired from the petitioner in Survey No.12/34 of Elampalloor Village within a time limit to be fixed by this Court.

3. The learned Special Government Pleader appearing for Revenue Department would submit that there is no laches on the part of the respondents in conducting auction in as much as even going by the averment in the writ petition the auction sale was notified on three occasions, but there was no bidders for the property.
The learned Government Pleader would further submit that the respondents are ready and willing to conduct public auction in respect of the property in question.

After hearing both sides, I am of the opinion that, the above writ petition could be disposed of as follows: There will be a direction to the 3 rd respondent to take steps to conduct auction sale of the property which was acquired from the petitioner comprised in Survey No.12/34 of Elampalloor Village, as expeditiously as possible, and to finalize the proceedings at any rate, within an outer limit of 6 months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
